Bakery Order DeskMonday DM sample

Project guide

Run the demo

  1. Open the dashboard and select Fetch DMs. If opening the page directly from disk, select the included Monday HTML file in the picker.
  2. Accept Jasmine or Patel individually, reject a request, or use Accept all and go to next day. Okafor has only one day of notice. Brown’s change and Moreau’s cancellation are applied at import.
  3. Book a helper on an eligible day. Its capacity increases from 8 to 12 hours, and weekly helper costs increase by $100.
  4. Advance to close the current day at 5 PM. Its accepted orders move to Picked up, and sales remain in the pickup week.

The demo starts on Monday, November 23, 2026. Progress is stored in this browser. The supplied wireframe provided the opening bookings and three new requests. The original Instagram file was unavailable, so the included sample recreates those requests and adds a change and cancellation. Fetch reads the sample file. Live Instagram access would require a connected Instagram account and a separate integration.

Wireframe and usability review

Current date          Fetch DMs | Accept all and go to next day
Today's pickups       New requests with pickup date and actions
Upcoming pickups      Booked time, time left, helper controls
Changes/cancellations Weekly sales and helper costs
Order history

The primary action stays by the simulated date. Each request shows its pickup date and eligibility beside its controls. Ineligible buttons have a visible reason. On narrow screens the two-column panels stack and the calendar wraps.

Order lifecycle

Fetch → Requested or Incompatible
Requested or Incompatible → Accepted when all checks pass
Requested or Incompatible → Rejected by the baker
Open order → Cancelled when notice passes
Accepted → Picked up at simulated 5 PM

Valid changes update the existing order. A move or change must meet notice for both dates and fit the destination oven capacity. The app excludes the original order from the capacity check. Pending requests do not reserve oven time. Bulk acceptance rechecks each request in receipt order, so a previously eligible request can become incompatible. Booking a helper can make a capacity-blocked request eligible.

Data model

Day [date]  1 ─── many  Order [id, pickup date]
Order      1 ─── many  DM [id, order reference]

Orders store customer, product, quantity, pickup date, request date, and status. Helper bookings store the date. The inbox stores each processed DM and its outcome. The product catalog defines prices and oven minutes once. Day capacity, order counts, oven load, sales, and helper costs are derived from these records.

Before importing Monday’s sample, Friday has 5 hours booked and 3 hours left. The opening week has $1,880 in sales and $0 in helper costs.

Import format

Import a JSON array, or an HTML file containing that array in a script element with the ID instagram-messages and type application/json. Refer to the sample for the field names. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Quantities are whole cakes or dozens of cupcakes. Changes and cancellations reference an existing order ID, which is the original DM ID for imported orders. Seed order IDs are lowercase customer names. To process a future-dated file, import it again on or after its send date.

Regression tests

From the bakery-orders folder, run node --test. The suite covers imports, notice and capacity boundaries, bulk acceptance, changes and cancellations, helper booking, sales, and pickup transitions.
